body:
## Confirmed defect

Backup creation copies mode and timestamps but not file ownership.

- `src/files.rs:477-590` has no `fchown`/UID/GID preservation path.
- Mode is applied before data writing, so platforms may clear set-ID bits during later writes.
- `spec/08-files.md:143` promises owner/group preservation.
- `spec/16-test-plan.md:115` explicitly excludes UID/GID from comparison, so current qualification cannot detect the mismatch.

## Affected behavior and impact

Backups can have different ownership from the source, and requested set-ID mode bits may not survive. This is a compatibility and metadata-integrity defect, especially for privileged or shared-file workflows.

Confidence: **High** for missing ownership handling; exact set-ID behavior is platform/filesystem-dependent.

## Recommended work

Apply ownership according to an explicit privilege/error policy, write and sync the content, then apply the final mode and timestamps in an order that preserves the intended metadata.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Backup UID and GID match the source when permissions allow.
- [ ] Permission-denied ownership cases follow a documented policy and are surfaced appropriately.
- [ ] Final mode, including set-ID behavior, is asserted after content writes.
- [ ] Tests run in an isolated/root-capable CI job where necessary.
- [ ] The validation comparator no longer excludes ownership without an explicit reason.
title: Backup: preserve documented ownership and final mode/set-ID metadata
